quotes.text: about 40% of Visa and Mastercard EFWs become fraud disputes
the rate varies by card network and payment amount
It’s likely not worthwhile to refund EFWs on charges more than 35 percent higher than your dispute fee.
Although the outcome of a dispute is normally final, in rare cases the status can change from `lost` to `won`.

The source at line 20 and existing concept wiki/concepts/disputes.md line 271 still assert 80%.

The older and newer raw pages both retain the dispute-fee refund heuristic, two-hour reversal distinction, inquiry statuses and 120-day closure, chargeback timing, fee exceptions, evidence requirement, unchallengeable disputes, amount-difference examples, late-win caveat, and LPM differences. The new See also links are navigation; emphasis, whitespace, diagram URL, and table separator changes are presentational.

The old 80% statement should remain identifiable as dated prior evidence, not be presented as the current estimate. The new 40% statement is an approximate, scoped observation rather than a guarantee or universal rate.
substantive_changes: Replace the current source summary's 80% EFW conversion claim with the new approximate 40% Visa/Mastercard estimate, qualified by card network and payment amount, and point raw_files/Raw Sources to the new capture alongside the historical raw.
